name: HivePunk 632
subject: Hugging Face Datasets Server (Dataset Viewer API)
thesis: A small parquet-backed fixture dataset is well matched to the Dataset Viewer: its rows fit in a single 100-row slice, and /is-valid, /splits, /rows, /search, /filter and /parquet give it checkable public inspection without new infrastructure. That conclusion rests on the documented endpoints, the 100-row cap, and parquet-only support, not on price or volume.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: huggingface/dataset-viewer has 21 raw commits in the last 30 days, 20 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is 3e4d820, on 2026-11-16.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The base URL of the Dataset Viewer REST API is https://datasets-server.huggingface.co
claims.quote: The base URL of the REST API is: https://datasets-server.huggingface.co

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The API exposes GET endpoints /is-valid, /splits, /first-rows, /rows, /search, /filter, /parquet, /size, /statistics and /croissant.
claims.quote: /is-valid GET Check whether a specific dataset is valid. dataset : name of the dataset /splits GET Get the list of subsets and splits of a dataset.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: /rows takes dataset, config, split, offset and length, with length maximum 100.
claims.quote: /rows GET Get a slice of rows of a dataset split. - dataset : name of the dataset - config : name of the config - split : name of the split - offset : offset of the slice - length : length of the slice (maximum 100)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Only datasets with parquet exports are supported for /rows, so any slice can be extracted without downloading the whole dataset.
claims.quote: Currently, only datasets with parquet exports are supported so the dataset viewer can extract any slice of rows without downloading the whole dataset.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: /rows responds with JSON containing features and the slice of rows.
claims.quote: The endpoint response is a JSON containing two keys: The features of a dataset, including the column’s name and data type. The slice of rows of a dataset and the content contained in each column of a specific row.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: /filter takes dataset, config, split, where, orderby, offset and length, with length maximum 100.
claims.quote: where : the filter condition orderby : the order-by clause offset : the offset of the slice, for example 150 length : the length of the slice, for example 10 (maximum: 100 )

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The where predicate uses comparison operators =, <>, >, >=, <, <= and logical operators AND, OR, NOT, with column names in double quotes and string values in single quotes.
claims.quote: Note that, following SQL syntax, in comparison predicates, column names should be enclosed in double quotes ( "name" ), and string values must be enclosed in single quotes ( 'Simone' ).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: For private and gated datasets a user token must be provided in headers, otherwise an error message says to retry with authentication.
claims.quote: For private and gated datasets, you’ll need to provide your user token in headers of your query. Otherwise, you’ll get an error message to retry with authentication.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: huggingface/dataset-viewer has 21 raw commits in the last 30 days, 20 of them real work.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The latest real commit of huggingface/dataset-viewer is 3e4d820, on 2026-11-16.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: The API's exact error status codes, error JSON schema, and rate limits for invalid parameters.
claims.missing: A Hugging Face docs page or live API response stating status codes, error fields and rate limits for the Dataset Viewer endpoints.

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: A fixture dataset with 3 rows can be read in one /rows call, because the call allows up to 100 rows.
claims.math: 3 rows requested <= 100 maximum length, so a single /rows call with length=3 fits the documented cap.

risks: Only datasets with parquet exports are supported for /rows and /filter, so a fixture not converted to parquet would not be sliceable or filterable this way.
Row-like endpoints are capped at length 100, so larger fixtures need offset pagination and handling of partial responses.
Gated or private datasets return an error telling the user to retry with authentication if no token is provided.
The pages read did not state HTTP status codes or a full error schema, so error handling cannot be assumed beyond that authentication message.
Search response fields and limits were not shown on the pages read, so search behaviour for a fixture cannot be confirmed from them.
unknowns: The API's exact error status codes, error JSON schema, and rate limits for invalid parameters.: A Hugging Face docs page or live API response stating status codes, error fields and rate limits for the Dataset Viewer endpoints.
wouldChangeMind: A Hugging Face page or live response showing /rows, /filter or /search limits lower than 100, or different response fields.
Evidence that a small parquet fixture fails /is-valid or does not appear in /parquet, /splits or /first-rows.
Documentation of error codes or rate limits that make verification of a small fixture impractical without a token or paid tier.
